title: In This Town, You Never Cross the Bridge in the Dark

lines.text: In this town, you only cross the old bridge with a lit lantern.
If your flame goes out halfway,
the Toll takes you.
Nobody has ever seen the Toll. Only what it leaves behind.
Mr. Okafor's flame died halfway across.
In the morning, his lantern was still on the planks.
So everyone checks their wick before they cross.
And there's one more rule, carved at the foot of the bridge.
One flame, one crossing.
The Toll counts flames, not people.
Two people under one light, and one of them stays.
My little brother Sam was six, and he hated that bridge.
Every evening, we crossed it home from Grandma's.
And every evening, I checked both our lanterns twice.
One night, the wind came up off the river.
Sam held my hand so tight it hurt.
Halfway across, his flame went out.
The water went completely still.
And something pale curled over the railing behind him.
There was only one flame now.
And two of us.
So I pushed my lantern into his hands.
Run. Don't look back.
He ran, and the light got smaller and smaller.
Until I was standing alone in the dark.
Sam made it to the other side.
And the Toll never took me.
It let me stay.
Because that's what the Toll is. Someone who gave their light away.
Now I wait on the bridge, for every light that goes out.
